title: Determining the Benefit Credit Set Against One Charge
content:
## 1. What is set against the charge

Benefit credit on a Northbeam Circle Membership is set against one charge the member is holding, and the
amount set against it is the smaller of the credit standing under the named benefit that charge's kind calls
for and the part of that charge the member is left to meet.

## 2. The credit standing under a named benefit

The credit standing under a named benefit is the benefit credit granted under it in the twelve months ending
on the handling day less the benefit credit spent under it in that window, and it never falls below nothing.

## 3. Which named benefit a charge calls for

The named benefit a charge's kind calls for is the service credit where the charge is bench or on-site
repair labour, the installation credit where it is installation labour, the delivery credit where it is a
delivery charge and the haul-away credit where it is a haul-away charge.

## 4. The part of the charge the member is left to meet

The labour taken is the least labour billed on that service at its labour rate. No parts are taken. No
attendance charges are taken. Nothing is taken off for cover. There is no member's discount share. The whole
of what remains is met at the redemption headroom.

The part of the charge the member is left to meet is the labour taken, the parts taken and the attendance
charges taken on the TechWorks job the charge belongs to, less what cover has already met, then at the
member's discount share and then at the redemption headroom.

The order is fixed: the labour, the parts and the attendance charges are added, what cover has met is taken
off that sum, the discount share is applied once to the whole of the remainder rather than line by line, the
headroom is then applied to that, and only that final figure is rounded to the nearest cent; no intermediate
is rounded and the part the member is left to meet never falls below nothing.

## 5. Limits on the redemption

A benefit code that already has a redemption booked against the same charge reference is not redeemed a
second time. A credit is never set against tax, against dues, or against the price of merchandise bought as
goods.

## 6. The figure worked through on hypothetical inputs

Take a charge for bench repair labour on a job whose service bills a least labour of 132.00 at its labour
rate, and take for this illustration no parts, no attendance charges, nothing met by cover, no member's
discount share and the whole of what remains met at the headroom. The part the member is left to meet is
132.00. Take the ledger as carrying 78.00 granted under the service credit in the twelve months ending on
the handling day and nothing spent under it in that window, so the credit standing under that named benefit
is 78.00. The smaller of 78.00 and 132.00 is 78.00, and 78.00 is the money set against the charge.
